positions.as_written: Expect posterior horn symptoms in deep flexion and absence of findings in mid range testing.
Treat the thinness of the deep flexion literature as a limit on confidence rather than as reassurance.
Treat deep flexion as a design constraint with a stated cost.
Restore posterior condylar offset rather than accepting an approximation.
Expect the deep flexion contact area to be small, and choose the bearing accordingly.
Repair posterior horn roots where feasible, on deep flexion loading grounds.
